gloss: Edo (old name for Tokyo); Edo period

definitions.explanation: The historical name for what is now Tokyo. Used as the seat of the Tokugawa shogunate from 1603 to 1868.
The historical period when Japan was ruled by the Tokugawa shogunate. Often used as a modifier to describe things from that era.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}は{今|いま}の{東京|とうきょう}です。
{明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}のとき、{江戸|えど}は{東京|とうきょう}に{改名|かいめい}された。
examples.english: At the time of the Meiji Restoration, Edo was renamed to Tokyo.

examples.japanese: ガイドブックを{片手|かたて}に、かつての{江戸|えど}の{面影|おもかげ}が{残|のこ}る{場所|ばしょ}を{訪|たず}ねて{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: Guidebook in hand, I walked around visiting places where traces of old Edo remain.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には{侍|さむらい}がいた。
examples.english: There were samurai during the Edo period.

examples.japanese: この{城|しろ}は{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{初|はじ}めに{建|た}てられた。
examples.english: This castle was built at the beginning of the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {歌舞伎|かぶき}や{浮世絵|うきよえ}など、{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}に{発展|はってん}した{文化|ぶんか}は{今|いま}でも{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Culture that developed during the Edo period, such as kabuki and ukiyo-e, is still popular today.

notes:
{江戸|えど} was the old name for what is now {東京|とうきょう}. It served as the seat of the {徳川|とくがわ}{幕府|ばくふ} (Tokugawa shogunate) from 1603 to 1868, and the name was changed to {東京|とうきょう} at the {明治|めいじ}{維新|いしん}.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい} — the Edo period (1603–1868)
- {江戸|えど}{幕府|ばくふ} — the Edo shogunate (Tokugawa shogunate)
- {江戸|えど}{前|まえ} — Edomae; in the Edo style (especially sushi)
- {江戸|えど}{城|じょう} — Edo Castle (now the site of the Imperial Palace)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Edo period is one of the most important eras in Japanese history, known for over 250 years of relative peace, the development of urban culture, and Japan's policy of national isolation ({鎖国|さこく}). Many aspects of modern Japanese culture — kabuki, ukiyo-e, sushi — originated or flourished during this time.
